version.changelog: Clarify CLI vs library scope, complete flags, add triggers and guardrails

llm.summary: The skill is a straightforward document-to-Markdown helper, but users should understand it installs and runs an unpinned npm CLI and has optional cloud conversion modes.

dimensions.detail: Local file access is proportionate for document conversion; optional Azure flags and API-key environment variables are documented, though the artifact does not prominently explain that cloud modes may send document contents externally.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill discloses npm/global and npx install paths, but the package version is not pinned, so the executed CLI may change over time.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Instructions are scoped to document conversion and error handling; Chinese trigger phrases are usage examples rather than a hidden language policy.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence, privilege escalation, background service, memory modification, or tool hijacking behavior appears in the artifact; the only durable change is the disclosed optional global npm install.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is converting local files to Markdown using @covoyage/file2md, and the documented commands, supported formats, and workflow align with that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable running the @covoyage/file2md npm package in your environment. For sensitive documents, prefer a pinned or vetted package version and avoid Azure cloud flags unless you explicitly intend to send the document to those services.
llm.findings:
[RP1] expected: Accepted as a supply-chain caution: unpinned npx examples are present, but they invoke the same disclosed file2md package used for the skill's stated purpose rather than hidden or unrelated code.
[SQP-2] expected: Accepted as a disclosure gap: Azure Document Intelligence and Content Understanding options are documented, but users should be warned more clearly that cloud processing can transmit document contents.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded: the Chinese phrases appear to be trigger examples for multilingual use and do not impose a hidden locale requirement.
[T08] expected: Accepted as install-risk context: the npm package and npx execution are unpinned, but the dependency is plainly named, purpose-aligned, and not accompanied by deceptive or destructive instructions.
